title: Act as Me (Delegation)
markdown:
The **delegation** module (`openexecutive.delegation`) is **Act as me**: the one place the Executive writes *as* a person instead of as itself. Everywhere else it has its own Google account and bots and signs as itself. Here, and only when the person asks, it writes an email in their voice and saves it as a **draft in their own Gmail** for them to review and send. This phase only drafts — nothing in the module can send — and only the principal can turn it on. It is off by default, and off changes nothing: the prompts, tool lists and prompt caches are byte-identical to an install without it. ## Who can have it, and when it is offered `delegation.settings.can_delegate(person)` is the single rule for who may turn it on: for now, the principal (a non-archived team member flagged `is_principal`). The rails a teammate's mailbox would need don't exist yet — audit rows private to *that* person (a row is either visible to every signed-in user or private to the principal), principal-only guards on the persona and Council edit routes, and per-seat Gmail credentials. So everything is keyed by `person_id`, and widening that one function is what the teammate phase changes. A person turns it on for themselves (`PUT /delegation`); nobody turns it on for anyone else. The setting is one row per person in `delegation_settings`, and a missing, unreadable or zero row all mean off. At the start of every chat turn (`Executive.stream_chat` and the committee path) `pin_turn_delegation(session, speaker_text)` runs next to the workspace-mode pin and records a `TurnDelegation` on the session. `ghostwrite_email` is **offered** only when all of these hold: - the speaker may have it and turned it on — read fresh every turn, so turning it off applies from the next message; - the speaker is the principal on a surface that verified it is them (`people_tools.is_principal_on_verified_surface`), and a web turn also carried a signed-in caller (`Session.web_caller_signed_in`, set from `x-caller-email`) or runs under local login — a request with no caller header is not a sign-in and never gets it (whoever holds the shared secret is trusted as the UI proxy that stamps that header, as on every principal-only route); - the conversation is private to the speaker: the web chat, a Slack or Discord DM, or a verified private Telegram chat — never a shared channel or thread, where the draft's preview or the matching threads would be posted for everyone and other people's messages sit in the model's context; - the turn is neither unattended (the scheduler's proactive run) nor private to the principal (the email poller's turns), so inbound text can never reach it. The MCP server, workflows, reflection and research never carry it at all. The Gmail connection is deliberately **not** part of the offer: the handler checks it on every call and says how to fix it, so the cached tool prefix never flips when a token lapses. The pin lives in a context variable for the turn's task as well as on the session, so two turns running at once on one session (a second browser tab) each read their own. It also carries the speaker's own words for the turn (a new email may go to an address they just typed — the turn's message joins the history only once the turn ends), a per-turn draft count, and `touched_mail` (see Privacy). ## The tool: `ghostwrite_email` It lives in its own registry (`orchestrator.delegation_tools.DELEGATION_TOOLS` / `DELEGATION_TOOL_HANDLERS`), **never** `_ALL_SKILL_TOOLS`, so no other toolkit can carry it. On a turn it is offered to, the agent loop adds it to the pool *before* the sort and builds that turn's handler map from both registries; on any other turn a call to it is an unknown tool. The handler re-checks the pin and the surface anyway, then: 1. **Caps** — at most 5 drafts per turn, and `DELEGATION_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_DAY` (default 50, at most 1000) per person per UTC day, counted from its own `delegation_drafted` audit rows, with a count kept in the process as a floor in case an audit row was lost. Each slot is taken before the first await — a round's tool calls run concurrently, so otherwise every call in it would pass the caps before any counted — and handed back if nothing was drafted. If the rows can't be read it refuses rather than guess. 2. **Marks the turn** — sets `TurnDelegation.touched_mail` *before* its first read of the mailbox. 3. **Checks the mailbox** — `gmail_status` asks Google whose mailbox the credential opens and compares it with the person's People email, on every call: a roster email can change, and a client slot swaps the roster. 4. **Finds the thread** — by `thread_id`, or a Gmail search (`find`). Several matches return `{status: "choose", candidates}` (subject, sender and date — no message text) and draft nothing; none returns `not_found`. 5. **Sets the recipients in code**, never from the model. A reply goes to the last inbound message's `From` — never its `Reply-To` (a different one is flagged `reply_to_ignored`) — with the thread's other recipients only on `reply_all`. A new email goes only to someone on the roster (contacts only when `contacts_reachable_now()`), or to an address the speaker typed this turn. Mailing-list mail, a thread they replied to last and a reply-all trimmed to 10 recipients are flagged. An address inside a block an adapter added to their message (the backstory hydrated into a DM) is not one they typed, and when the message carries an attachment — a document's inlined text, or a note naming the file — none of its addresses count: neither has an end mark, and a filename is chosen by whoever sent the file. They give the address in a message of its own. 6. **Writes it** (the ghostwriter, below) and saves it with `DelegateGmail.create_draft`, threaded with `In-Reply-To`, `References` (whole message ids: when the chain is too long for one header the oldest after the thread's first go, never the parent) and `threadId`, and stamped `X-OE-Ghostwritten`. The result is `{status: "drafted", draft_id, gmail_link, to, cc, subject, preview, flags, open_questions, note}`. The link is built server-side from a fixed Gmail prefix, and the note tells the model the preview is the person's draft, to be treated as data. The chat shows an action chip — "Drafted an email as you to … — in your Gmail Drafts" — that opens it in Gmail. A sincere "are you an AI?" in the thread comes back as an open question for the person to answer themselves. ## The ghostwriter `delegation.ghostwriter.compose` writes the text. The Executive decides *what* to say (`intent`); this call decides *how* the person would say it, and it is deliberately small: - a constant `GHOSTWRITER_PROMPT` plus the person's voice block as the system prompt; - the thread (each message cut to its sender's own words, every line scrubbed), the intent and the recipients' names in the user turn — no company profile, memory or roster; - **no tools** but the forced `compose_reply` return, so text in the thread can ask for anything and there is nothing to do it with. It is not a Council agent — the Council's edit routes have no principal check — and runs on `DELEGATION_COMPOSER_MODEL` (default: the default model), logged as `ghostwriter` usage. `lint` then runs in code on what comes back: a link or an email address survives only if it appears in the intent, the signature or the recipients, so a link planted in the thread is removed and flagged; the Executive's own name is flagged; and the body is capped, cut at a paragraph, line or word break in its last fifth. A draft with nothing left after that is refused. The signature from the person's Gmail settings is appended. ## How I write `delegation.voice` learns how a person writes *their own* email (`attunement.style` learns how the Executive should write *to* someone). `POST /delegation/voice/learn` reads up to 40 recent sent messages, keeps only what they wrote (quoted replies stripped with the email poller's `sender_new_text`), skips automatic mail and every thread it drafted into, and makes one forced-tool call (`record_voice_profile`). Code validates every field before it is stored: - greetings per audience (their team, their contacts, anyone else), a sign-off of at most two lines, and a usual length and tone (a backslash-n the model wrote instead of a line break is read as one, keeping the first lines that fit, which also repairs a profile stored before that rule); - up to 8 habits and 6 things to avoid, through the same deny-list as working-style rules — no actions, links, handles, amounts, tool names or names of people; - up to 3 short exemplars, each checked to be verbatim from a sample, with addresses and phone numbers masked — and none while a client slot is active, so one client's mail never lands in another's state. The signature comes from Gmail's `sendAs` settings, not the model, as plain text with its lines kept (`gmail.html_to_text`: a `
` always ends a line, and a block tag, opening or closing, ends one when it has text, so Gmail's layout of a first line followed by one `
` per line comes out line by line). `POST /delegation/voice/signature` reads it again without relearning: nothing else changes and a locked profile stays locked, so it picks up a changed Gmail signature and undoes **Don't add my signature**. The person can edit the profile, lock it (a locked profile is never relearned) and reset it, and every change is kept in `delegation_voice_history`. One learn runs at a time per person, and a lock or an edit made while it runs wins: the learned profile is dropped (`changed`). ## The mailbox client `delegation.gmail.DelegateGmail` talks to the Gmail REST API directly and is **never registered with the MCP gateway**, so the model reaches the mailbox only through the typed handler. The credential is one file per person in `DELEGATION_GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_DIR`, named from a hash of the address (0600 in a 0700 directory), minted by `scripts/connect-own-gmail.py` on the Executive's own OAuth client with the scopes `gmail.readonly` and `gmail.compose`. It never lives in `WORKSPACE_MCP_CREDENTIALS_DIR`, where workspace-mcp picks a credential by address. There is **no send method** — a unit test fails if one appears. `gmail_status` answers `connected`, `not_configured`, `needs_reconnect` (Google refused the saved sign-in — an app in Testing mode has its tokens expire after 7 days; a rate limit, though Gmail may send it as a 403, is an `error` to retry, not a reconnect), `mismatch`, `no_email`, `shared_mailbox` or `error`. `shared_mailbox` means the person's address *is* the Executive's; it is refused before asking Google, because then everything the Executive writes would look like theirs. The gateway closes the other door: every `google_workspace__*` call must act as the Executive's own account, and a `user_google_email` naming anyone else is refused and audited (see Integrations). ## Privacy Once `touched_mail` is set, every audit row the turn writes is private to the principal (`people_tools.audit_row_private_to_principal`): the tool row (its input and result redacted, since `ghostwrite` is a sensitive tool name), the reply's `chat_turn` row that carries the preview, the model-call rows, and the background passes, which run under `private_rows`. The Honcho peer and department syncs are skipped, because peer memory is read on other people's turns. No memory is learned from the turn at all: the episodic, open-loop and working-style passes are skipped too, since its reply quotes a draft built from other people's mail. The four `delegation_*` audit events are always private and carry metadata only — ids, counts and flags, never the draft or the thread. ## The system prompt A constant, name-free `DELEGATION_ADDENDUM` joins block 0 after the unchanged identity addendum while anyone on the install has it on (`block0_delegation_on`). It tells the model that `ghostwrite_email` is the single exception to *never impersonate*, and only for the person being spoken to; that everything else is written as itself; that when the tool isn't offered the asker can't have it; that a draft is never described as sent; and that it never denies being an AI. It is keyed on the install-level setting, never on the turn or the speaker, so switching it misses the 1h cache once (see Prompt Caching). ## Surfaces - **Settings → Act as me** (`ActAsMeCard`, hidden unless `GET /delegation` answers): the Gmail connection with the connect command and **Check again**, the **Write drafts as me** switch, and **How I write**: length and tone, a greeting per audience (`{first}` is their first name), the sign-off, habits and never-rules in fields that grow to show every line, the signature with **Refresh from Gmail** and **Don't add my signature** (or **Add my Gmail signature** when none is added), and each example quoted with **Remove examples**. - **Setup status**: a **Your own Gmail (Act as me)** light (`your_gmail`). - **API**: `GET`/`PUT /delegation`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /delegation/voice`, `POST /delegation/voice/learn` and `POST /delegation/voice/signature` — the caller's own delegation only (see API Reference). - **Evals**: a scenario's `delegation:` block runs the turn against an in-memory mailbox (`evals.mailbox.ScenarioMailbox`) and hands the saved drafts to the judge (`delegation_001`–`003`). Sending — after a tap, or within rules the person sets — and teammates having their own are later, separate changes, each behind its own switch, off by default.
